report.root_cause: Order-gateway 2.4.0 deployed under CHG-4310 (connection pooling changes) caused memory growth and GC pauses on order-gateway-2, which drove the latency in ALR-1001. The matching-engine and reference-db were not the cause, and the operator's requested matching-engine restart was not performed.
report.summary: Network and database checks ruled out the link to matching-engine and reference-db, pointing to heap pressure on order-gateway-2 after CHG-4310. Remediation rolled back CHG-4310 (ACT-001, 11:17), and order-gateway-2 later hit OutOfMemoryError at 11:22 and restarted, after which the reviewer confirmed latency at about 5 ms and error rate at 0.001; the heap growth root cause still needs follow-up because it could recur.

report.root_cause: order-gateway-2 had heap/memory pressure from a leak-like heap climb (90% to about 98%) that caused repeated GC pauses of up to 810 ms and latency of about 400 ms. CHG-4310 (order-gateway 2.4.0, connection pooling changes) is the candidate trigger but is not confirmed as the cause, and it remains active. reference-db was ruled out by the database check.
report.summary: The network specialist (H-004) traced the latency_high alert on order-gateway (ALR-1001) to order-gateway-2 heap pressure, not the network or reference-db, and remediation (H-006) isolated and restarted only that instance, bringing its latency to 5.0 ms and memory to about 55%. The reviewer (H-008) confirmed service latency of 5.5 ms and error rate 0.001 at 11:25, but noted that order-gateway-2 heap is climbing again (55.3% to 57.1%) and CHG-4310 was not rolled back, so the recovery is not yet proven durable and needs monitoring or a rollback decision.

report.root_cause: Probable root cause is network ACL update CHG-4750 (order-gateway site A to reference-db, applied 10:08). Its ACL reload raised the order-gateway to reference-db round trip from about 3 ms to 190 ms, while reference-db server-side metrics stayed flat at 2.0 ms, so the delay is on the network path, not in the database. Planned maintenance MRX-4790 (reference-db site B offline 10:00-13:00) was a separate factor and was not the cause; the network specialist suspected retries toward reference-db-2 but could not confirm that.
report.summary: Remediation rolled back CHG-4750 at 10:50 (ACT-001), and order-gateway latency was reported at 5.0 ms at 10:51, but the reviewer could not confirm recovery because the tool-call limits blocked all post-rollback checks, so INC-1 and ALR-1001 are not confirmed as resolved. The specialists' constraints were respected throughout: no failover to site B, no traffic steered to reference-db-2 until 13:00, and reference-db-1 capacity was not verified. Next step is to re-run read-only checks on order-gateway and reference-db latency, error rate, ALR-1001 state, and CHG-4750 status once tool access is restored.

The database side reports reference-db healthy at 2 ms, and the conflicting MRX-4790 status on reference-db-2 is unresolved.
report.summary: Rolling back CHG-4310 at 10:44 did not clear the incident: the reviewer reports order-gateway aggregate latency still at 225 ms against a 20 ms limit and order-gateway-1 reference-db round trips of 180-806 ms after the rollback, with the order-gateway to reference-db link degraded at 10:50. The reviewer could not verify ALR-1001 or the CX-12 link state, and the follow-up read-only check was blocked by an exhausted tool budget, so the incident stays open and needs the network team (CX-12) and the dba-team (MRX-4790, reference-db-2) before anyone treats it as cleared.

report.root_cause: CHG-4801, applied to reference-db at 10:27, lowered max_connections from 400 to 120. Once that limit was reached, reference-db refused new connections, and order-gateway-1 began returning 503 'reference-db refused connection (max_connections)'. The network and database findings agree on this cause, and CHG-4801 is still active.
report.summary: Order rejections on order-gateway (ALR-1001) continue because CHG-4801 still caps reference-db max_connections at 120. The fix is to roll back CHG-4801 to 400, but that is a reference-db action and no incident-manager approval has been granted, so remediation has not run and the reviewer has not confirmed recovery. An incident manager needs to approve the rollback of CHG-4801 before recovery can be confirmed; the database and network reports also conflict on whether the 503s stopped after 10:28, which the reviewer reports as ongoing through 10:57.

This is a hypothesis: the network specialist's log reads were blocked by the tool-call limit, so the cause is not confirmed from logs. reference-db was ruled out (healthy, no CHG-... or MRX-... found), and ALR-1001 was not directly examined.
report.summary: Remediation ACT-001 isolated (drained) order-gateway-2 at 10:28, which brought the order-gateway error rate back to 0.1%, but the incident is not over: order-gateway-1 is now carrying all flow, queue_depth has risen every tick (15 to 75) and latency is climbing toward the 20 ms limit (12.5 ms at 10:31), with the trading session still open. CHG-4310 was not rolled back because its rollback eligibility and the drain/restart constraints were never verified, so a human needs to decide on CHG-4310 rollback or restarting order-gateway-2 and to investigate the queue growth on order-gateway-1 before INC-9101 and ALR-1001 can be closed.

report.summary: INC-9101 is unresolved: the reviewer confirmed at 10:22 that the storm was ongoing, and at 10:27 order-gateway-2 was still exiting from OutOfMemoryError while order-gateway-1 remained healthy at 5ms. No mitigation was applied because isolating order-gateway-2 needs confirmation that no order-gateway maintenance window exists (none found in a log search, but the ticket system was not checked for it) and any CHG-4310 rollback needs change-control approval, so someone with ticket access should confirm the window and approve isolating order-gateway-2 so order-gateway-1 carries the load.
